title: Valera and Antique Items
statementMd:
Valera is a collector. Once he wanted to expand his collection with exactly one antique item.

Valera knows $*n*$ sellers of antiques, the $*i*$-th of them auctioned $*k*_{*i*}$ items. Currently the auction price of the $*j*$-th object of the $*i*$-th seller is $*s*_{*ij*}$. Valera gets on well with each of the $*n*$ sellers. He is perfectly sure that if he outbids the current price of one of the items in the auction (in other words, offers the seller the money that is strictly greater than the current price of the item at the auction), the seller of the object will immediately sign a contract with him.

Unfortunately, Valera has only $*v*$ units of money. Help him to determine which of the $*n*$ sellers he can make a deal with.

## Input

The first line contains two space-separated integers $*n*, *v*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 50; 10^{4} ≤ *v* ≤ 10^{6})$ — the number of sellers and the units of money the Valera has.

Then $*n*$ lines follow. The $*i*$-th line first contains integer $*k*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *k*_{*i*} ≤ 50)$ the number of items of the $*i*$-th seller. Then go $*k*_{*i*}$ space-separated integers $*s*_{*i*1}, *s*_{*i*2}, ..., *s*_{*ik*_{*i*}}$ $(10^{4} ≤ *s*_{*ij*} ≤ 10^{6})$ — the current prices of the items of the $*i*$-th seller.

## Output

In the first line, print integer $*p*$ — the number of sellers with who Valera can make a deal.

In the second line print $*p*$ space-separated integers $*q*_{1}, *q*_{2}, ..., *q*_{*p*}$ $(1 ≤ *q*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$ — the numbers of the sellers with who Valera can make a deal. Print the numbers of the sellers **in the increasing order**.

## Note

In the first sample Valera can bargain with each of the sellers. He can outbid the following items: a $40000$ item from the first seller, a $20000$ item from the second seller, and a $10000$ item from the third seller.

In the second sample Valera can not make a deal with any of the sellers, as the prices of all items in the auction too big for him.
statementZhMd:
瓦列拉是一名收藏家。有一次，他想要正好购买一件古董来扩充自己的收藏。

瓦列拉认识 $*n*$ 位古董卖家，其中第 $*i*$ 位卖家拍卖了 $*k*_{*i*}$ 件物品。目前，第 $*i*$ 位卖家所拍卖的第 $*j*$ 件物品的价格为 $*s*_{*ij*}$。瓦列拉与这 $*n*$ 位卖家中的每一位关系都很好。他非常确定，如果他对拍卖中的某件物品出价高于当前价格（换句话说，向卖家支付严格高于该物品当前拍卖价格的钱），该物品的卖家就会立即与他签订合同。

不幸的是，瓦列拉只有 $*v*$ 单位的钱。请帮助他确定可以与这 $*n*$ 位卖家中的哪些人达成交易。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*, *v*$ $(1 ≤ *n* ≤ 50; 10^{4} ≤ *v* ≤ 10^{6})$ —— 卖家的数量以及瓦列拉拥有的钱数。

接下来有 $*n*$ 行。第 $*i*$ 行首先包含整数 $*k*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *k*_{*i*} ≤ 50)$，表示第 $*i*$ 位卖家拥有的物品数量。接下来是 $*k*_{*i*}$ 个用空格分隔的整数 $*s*_{*i*1}, *s*_{*i*2}, ..., *s*_{*ik*_{*i*}}$ $(10^{4} ≤ *s*_{*ij*} ≤ 10^{6})$ —— 第 $*i*$ 位卖家所售物品的当前价格。

## 输出格式

第一行输出整数 $*p*$ —— 瓦列拉可以与之达成交易的卖家数量。

第二行输出 $*p*$ 个用空格分隔的整数 $*q*_{1}, *q*_{2}, ..., *q*_{*p*}$ $(1 ≤ *q*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$ —— 瓦列拉可以与之达成交易的卖家编号。请按**递增顺序**输出卖家编号。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，瓦列拉可以与每一位卖家进行交易。他可以对以下物品出价高于当前价格：第一位卖家的 $40000$ 物品、第二位卖家的 $20000$ 物品以及第三位卖家的 $10000$ 物品。

在第二个样例中，瓦列拉无法与任何卖家达成交易，因为拍卖中所有物品的价格都太高了。
